title: The Industry 5.0 Fallacy: The Premature Mortality of Industry 4.0
content: Part of the literature labels Industry 5.0 (I5.0), built on human-centricity, sustainability and resilience, a Fifth Industrial Revolution, although the European Commission, which gave the term its official definition, does not present it as a successor to Industry 4.0 (I4.0) despite adopting the incremented number. This paper argues that I5.0 is a goal-level redirection of a still largely unrealized I4.0, not a new industrial revolution. The argument is a systems argument. I4.0, defined as a network of cyber-physical, fractal, distributed nodes forming a Fractal–Complex Adaptive System (CAS), extends plant-level adaptiveness from people to machinery, with the closed digital-twin loop as the internal model that anticipates the consequences of actions and is corrected when its predictions fail. A revolution accordingly denotes a change in the structure of the production system, not in the goals it serves; by that criterion I5.0 is not one. A second claim is that declaring any successor is premature: a genealogy of changeability shows that I4.0 consolidates decades of manufacturing-systems research, and adoption indicators (189 recognized lighthouse sites, low maturity indices and digital twins that rarely close the loop) show it far from realized. Its neglected ecological and social pillars belong on I4.0’s agenda.
